1: NATALYA STEPANOVNA. Papa, tell us truly, which is the better dog, our Squeezer or his Guess.
2: LOMOV. Stepan Stepanovitch, I implore you to tell me just one thing: is your Squeezer overshot or not? Yes or no?
3: CHUBUKOV. And suppose he is? What does it matter? He's the best dog in the district for all that, and so on.
4: LOMOV. But isn't my Guess better? Really, now?
5: CHUBUKOV. Don't excite yourself, my precious one.... Allow me.... Your Guess certainly has his good points.... He's pure-bred, firm on his feet, has well-sprung ribs, and all that. But, my dear man, if you want to know the truth, that dog has two defects: he's old and he's short in the muzzle.
6: LOMOV. Excuse me, my heart.... Let's take the facts.... You will remember that on the Marusinsky hunt my Guess ran neck-and-neck with the Count's dog, while your Squeezer was left a whole verst behind.
7: CHUBUKOV. He got left behind because the Count's whipper-in hit him with his whip.
8: LOMOV. And with good reason. The dogs are running after a fox, when Squeezer goes and starts worrying a sheep!
9: CHUBUKOV. It's not true!... My dear fellow, I'm very liable to lose my temper, and so, just because of that, let's stop arguing. You started because everybody is always jealous of everybody else's dogs. Yes, we're all like that! You too, sir, aren't blameless! You no sooner notice that some dog is better than your Guess than you begin with this, that... and the other... and all that.... I remember everything!
11: CHUBUKOV. [Teasing him] I remember, too.... What do you remember?
12: LOMOV. My heart... my foot's gone to sleep.... I can't...
13: NATALYA STEPANOVNA. [Teasing] My heart.... What sort of a hunter are you? You ought to go and lie on the kitchen oven and catch blackbeetles, not go after foxes! My heart!
14: CHUBUKOV. Yes really, what sort of a hunter are you, anyway? You ought to sit at home with your palpitations, and not go tracking animals. You could go hunting, but you only go to argue with people and interfere with their dogs and so on. Let's change the subject in case I lose my temper. You're not a hunter at all, anyway!
15: LOMOV. And are you a hunter? You only go hunting to get in with the Count and to intrigue.... Oh, my heart!... You're an intriguer!
16: CHUBUKOV. What? I an intriguer? [Shouts] Shut up!
20: CHUBUKOV. Shut up or I'll shoot you like a partridge! You fool!
21: LOMOV. Everybody knows that--oh my heart!--your late wife used to beat you.... My feet... temples... sparks.... I fall, I fall!
22: CHUBUKOV. And you're under the slipper of your housekeeper!
23: LOMOV. There, there, there... my heart's burst! My shoulder's come off.... Where is my shoulder? I die. [Falls into an armchair] A doctor! [Faints.]
24: CHUBUKOV. Boy! Milksop! Fool! I'm sick! [Drinks water] Sick!
25: NATALYA STEPANOVNA. What sort of a hunter are you? You can't even sit on a horse! [To her father] Papa, what's the matter with him? Papa! Look, papa! [Screams] Ivan Vassilevitch! He's dead!
26: CHUBUKOV. I'm sick!... I can't breathe!... Air!
27: NATALYA STEPANOVNA. He's dead. [Pulls LOMOV'S sleeve] Ivan Vassilevitch! Ivan Vassilevitch! What have you done to me? He's dead. [Falls into an armchair] A doctor, a doctor! [Hysterics.]
28: CHUBUKOV. Oh!... What is it? What's the matter?
30: CHUBUKOV. Who's dead? [Looks at LOMOV] So he is! My word! Water! A doctor! [Lifts a tumbler to LOMOV'S mouth] Drink this!... No, he doesn't drink.... It means he's dead, and all that.... I'm the most unhappy of men! Why don't I put a bullet into my brain? Why haven't I cut my throat yet? What am I waiting for? Give me a knife! Give me a pistol! [LOMOV moves] He seems to be coming round.... Drink some water! That's right....
32: LOMOV. I see stars... mist.... Where am I?
33: CHUBUKOV. Hurry up and get married and--well, to the devil with you! She's willing! [He puts LOMOV'S hand into his daughter's] She's willing and all that. I give you my blessing and so on. Only leave me in peace!
34: LOMOV. [Getting up] Eh? What? To whom?
35: CHUBUKOV. She's willing! Well? Kiss and be damned to you!
36: NATALYA STEPANOVNA. [Wails] He's alive... Yes, yes, I'm willing....
38: LOMOV. Eh? Kiss whom? [They kiss] Very nice, too. Excuse me, what's it all about? Oh, now I understand... my heart... stars... I'm happy. Natalya Stepanovna.... [Kisses her hand] My foot's gone to sleep....
39: NATALYA STEPANOVNA. I... I'm happy too....
40: CHUBUKOV. What a weight off my shoulders.... Ouf!
41: NATALYA STEPANOVNA. But... still you will admit now that Guess is worse than Squeezer.
44: CHUBUKOV. Well, that's a way to start your family bliss! Have some champagne!
47: CHUBUKOV. [Trying to shout her down] Champagne! Champagne! Curtain.
